findings.current: {count, plural, one {# घंटा पहले} other {# घंटे पहले}}
findings.problem: Before पहले ('ago') standard Hindi takes the oblique: 'एक घंटे पहले'; CLDR hi uses 'घंटे पहले' for one too. 'घंटा पहले' is common colloquially and matches shipped relay.notifications.age.hours, so it is not wrong, just less standard.
findings.fix: Optional: one {# घंटे पहले} other {# घंटे पहले}. If you change it, change relay.notifications.age.hours in the same wave so the two stay consistent. Otherwise keep as is. Does not gate.

findings.current: short.hours one {# घंटा}; due.ahead '{label} में' → '1 घंटा में'
findings.problem: The postposition में requires the oblique: '1 घंटे में'. dueLabel (schedules-copy.ts:114-141) passes short.hours count=1 into due.ahead when the due time is 90–119 min away, so '1 घंटा में' / 'अगली बार 1 घंटा में' is reachable. This is new in O3-a, because before it the token was the Latin '1h'. The bare uses (row stamp, '1 घंटा 05 मिनट') need the nominative, so short.hours itself is correct and cannot fix this.
findings.fix: Deferred to code/key: give dueLabel its own in-form (oblique) unit keys, or reword due.ahead into a form that takes the nominative. Do not change the short.hours one arm. Meaning stays clear; it is a one-count agreement slip in a 30-min window.

notes.C-ICU: PASS: every plural is one/other (CLDR hi; one = 0 and 1). The घंटा/घंटे and हफ़्ता/हफ़्ते nominative split is correct for bare durations. सेकंड/मिनट/दिन/साल are invariant. Placeholders, '#' count and the zero-padded {seconds}/{minutes} text are identical to en.
notes.C-KAL: PASS: कल ('yesterday'/'tomorrow') is unambiguous. Every consumer is past-only: inbox buckets (timeBucket, notifications-model.ts:131-141), Team Bridge day dividers for earlier messages (team-bridge/model.ts:529-530), and inbox row meta for days===1 (notifications-model.ts:530-532). No future-date copy appears on those surfaces. This matches standard Hindi UI usage and shipped relay.notifications.section.yesterday.
notes.C-WEEK: PASS: bucket.earlier_this_week 'पिछले कुछ दिन' ('the last few days') is a rolling phrase. It matches the 2–6-day window (atMs >= todayStart-6*DAY_MS and < yesterday start; notifications-model.ts:135-141) on any weekday, and avoids the calendar-week reading that was MAJOR in ru. It sits under आज/कल and above पहले, so it reads as 'before yesterday'.
notes.N1: Note only, code fix deferred: short.minutes_spaced/hours/days/weeks/years act as row-stamp ages (session-projection.ts:400-409; team-bridge/model.ts:611-624). In Hindi, a bare '5 मिनट' reads as a duration, not an age. That ambiguity matches English '5m', so it is no translation defect. A dedicated *_ago row-stamp key would remove it.
